newsitem.title: CHINA: China performers face final curtain on job security.
newsitem.headline: China performers face final curtain on job security.

text.p: China's performing artists are facing the final curtain on guaranteed jobs, and for the first time, some could soon be unemployed, officials said on Monday.
About 120 musicians, actors, singers and dancers who failed qualifying examinations could be out of a job in a move to bring market style reforms to the arts, Ministry of Culture officials said.
"They are among 3,000 who have taken qualifying examinations since the beginning of this year," one official told Reuters.
"They are not unemployed yet, they are being retrained," he said. "But if they do not find a new job they could be unemployed."
China had long given artists a guaranteed job, widely referred to as an "iron rice bowl." They were paid little, but the state made few demands on either their time or their skills.
But that has changed in recent years with the introduction of market style reforms.
The state is now cutting its subsidies to performing arts troupes, which are being forced to cut costs and raise money through ticket sales.
That has also meant that troupes now have to make sure that they need all of their employees, and that everyone on the payroll meets minimum standards.

The 3,000 given a qualifying examination were from 10 groups under the central government, including the China Symphonic Orchestra, the Central Song and Dance Troupe, the Central Opera and Ballet Academy and the Experimental Centre for Modern Drama.

"Although the number is small, these will be the first group of artists to face unemployment," the official Xinhua news agency quoted Jiang Fengyi, deputy director of the Ministry of Culture's personnel department, as saying.
